body.p:
NABARD seeks an Enterprise KYC/AML Solution to integrate with existing NABARD applications and implement a complete digital KYC, KYB, and CKYC workflow through CKYCRR (CERSAI). The Bidder shall be responsible for design, supply, configuration, customization, integration, testing, deployment, security hardening, and ongoing support of the solution. The solution shall provide due diligence capabilities including customer acceptance, customer identification procedure, customer due diligence, beneficial owner identification (for entities), ongoing due diligence triggers, automated regulatory compliance flows, and audit ready evidence and reporting as per regulatory and Bank’s KYC/AML policy. 1.
Standards based Integration:

The Bidder shall provide API/Web-SDK or other applicable standards based integration so that NABARD applications (web portals, internal systems, and authentication services such as Active Directory/SSO where applicable) can invoke KYC/KYB/CKYC services. Integration shall support initiation, status retrieval, decision outcomes, evidence retrieval, and master record updates. 1.1.
The solution shall adhere to enterprise architecture principles including
modularity, scalability, interoperability, and reusability across NABARD systems.
The solution shall be implemented as a shared enterprise service layer consumable by multiple NABARD applications 1.2.
The solution shall enforce separation of concerns across presentation, business logic, integration, and data layers. 1.3.

2.4.

sec.title: 4.1 User Management & Access Control
sec.p:
4.1.1
The Bidder shall implement role-based access with defined user types
(initiator/maker-checker, compliance reviewer, administrator, auditor, view only).

4.1.2
The Bidder shall implement configurable maker-checker workflows for
actions with configurable approval hierarchies and escalation paths.

4.1.3
The Bidder shall ensure immutable audit trails for creation, modification,
approval/rejection, overrides, and record access.

sec.title: 4.2 Integration with NABARD Systems
sec.p:
4.2.1
The Bidder shall integrate the solution through APIs/SDKs with
NABARD applications and portals for initiation, status retrieval, and posting of verified KYC/KYB/CKYC outcomes.

4.2.2
The Bidder shall support integration with NABARD employee
authentication services (e.g., directory-based authentication/SSO) and role management, as applicable.

4.2.3
The Bidder shall integrate with NABARD SMS and Email gateways
(provided by NABARD) for OTPs, alerts, and transactional notifications.

4.2.4
The Bidder shall provide the capability to generate a KYC session via API
call and create a URL/QR code to launch the KYC journey; the journey shall be resumable later and on another supported device or browser session.

4.2.5
The Bidder shall expose all integration APIs through a secured API
gateway layer (provided by NABARD), with enforced authentication, authorization, request validation, and protection against common API threats.
APIs shall adhere to open standards and be documented using Open API/Swagger specifications to ensure interoperability and avoid vendor lock-in. 4.2.5.1

4.2.5.2
The Bidder shall implement explicit API security controls for all
internal and external APIs, services, connectors, SDK interfaces, and integration interfaces forming part of the solution.

4.2.5.3
Such controls shall include authentication, authorization, request

and payload validation, schema validation, encryption in transit, rate limiting, throttling, abuse protection, secure error handling, replay protection where applicable, and comprehensive logging and monitoring.

4.2.5.4
These controls shall apply, inter alia, to integrations with
CKYCRR/CERSAI, sanctions/watchlist screening services,
verification utilities, and all NABARD internal and external system interfaces.

4.2.6
Without prejudice to the API security controls set out above, the Bidder

shall specifically ensure that rate-limiting, throttling, and abuse protection controls are enforced for sensitive and high-volume API endpoints, including session creation, status calls, evidence retrieval, and bulk/batch operations.

4.2.7
The Bidder shall ensure secure system-to-system communication
between NABARD applications and the solution using TLS encryption; where applicable, mutual authentication (mTLS) shall be supported for trusted applications/services.

4.2.8
The Bidder shall ensure that API requests and responses do not log or
expose sensitive identifiers (e.g., Aadhaar, PAN) in raw form; masking/redaction shall be enforced for logs, exports, and diagnostics.

4.2.9
The Bidder shall provide versioned APIs/SDKs with a defined versioning
approach to support upgrades without disruption to NABARD consuming applications.

4.2.10
The Bidder shall support asynchronous status updates through secure
callbacks/webhooks (where required) for long-running operations (e.g., CKYC fetch, batch processing, verification outcomes), along with retry and failure handling.

4.2.10.1
The solution shall support event-driven architecture by
publishing key lifecycle events (e.g., KYC completion, CKYC updates, risk category changes, Re-KYC triggers) through an enterprise messaging/event streaming platform.

The Bidder shall provide an integration kit for NABARD applications, including API specifications, sample payloads, error codes, and sandbox/UAT enablement artefacts for integration testing. 4.2.11

4.2.12
The Bidder shall ensure that access (digital or physical) by vendor
personnel, if any, is KYC compliant.

4.2.13
All external integrations (CKYCRR, UIDAI, MCA, etc.) shall be

sec.title: 4.3 KYC/KYB Onboarding Journeys
sec.p:
4.3.1
The Bidder shall provide configurable onboarding journeys for both
individual customers (KYC) and business entities (KYB). The solution shall support the design and modification of onboarding workflows in alignment with NABARD’s business requirements, regulatory
obligations, and operational processes, without requiring significant code-level changes.

The solution shall incorporate dynamic and configurable data capture forms that automatically adapt based on the customer type, product category, and assigned risk classification. The forms shall enable conditional field display, validation rules, document requirements, and workflow routing, ensuring that relevant information is collected efficiently and in compliance with applicable regulatory guidelines. 4.3.1.1

4.3.2
The Bidder shall support assisted and self-serve modes with configurable
intake channels, including web-based and mobile-responsive browser-based access, as well as assisted desk operations.

4.3.3
The proposed KYC/AML solution is expected to support onboarding and

due diligence workflows for a diverse set of client/customer categories handled by NABARD, including but not limited to individuals, proprietary concerns, partnership firms, companies (public/private), trusts, societies, NGOs/NPOs, Government and Government-owned entities, banks, NBFCs, co-operative institutions, SHGs/JLGs, farmer groups, universities, and other juridical persons.

4.3.4
The Bidder shall implement a comprehensive KYB authentication

framework for non-individual entities, including Companies, Firms, NGOs, Co-operatives, SHGs/JLGs, Government bodies, and other similar entities, ensuring multi-level authentication at the entity, authorized signatory, and Beneficial Ownership levels. The solution shall support validation of key identifiers such as PAN, GSTIN (including PAN–GST mapping and status verification), and Legal Entity Identifier (LEI), along with lifecycle management, through authorized and verifiable sources. The solution shall further enable authentication of authorized signatories through individual KYC mechanisms, validation of authorization documents (such as Board Resolutions and mandate/Power of Attorney), and establishment of linkage with verified Beneficial Owners. Category-specific authentication workflows shall be supported, including NGO Darpan validation, registrar-based verification, and assisted authentication mechanisms for SHGs/JLGs and other rural entities. The

The solution shall generate Unique Customer Identification Code (UCIC)
and perform deduplication at enterprise level.

4.3.9
The solution shall maintain a relationship model linking entity,

authorized signatories, directors / partners / trustees / office bearers, beneficial owners, and associated facilities / accounts, and such relationships shall be consumable by onboarding, screening, risk scoring, Re-KYC, and AML investigation workflows.

4.3.10
For the purpose of customer identification and due diligence, the

solution shall support verification of documents and information as per prevailing guidelines. The onboarding process may typically involve verification of a combination of documents such as Officially Valid Documents (OVDs) (as defined under RBI Master Direction on KYC) for identity and address proof, Permanent Account Number (PAN) or equivalent declarations, and such other documents as may be required to establish legal existence, business activity, ownership structure, and financial profile of the customer/entity.
For non-individual entities, onboarding may further include verification of entity-specific documents such as registration/incorporation 4.3.11
certificates, constitutional documents (e.g., partnership deed,

memorandum/articles, trust deed), authorization documents, and identification of beneficial owners and authorized signatories, along with their individual KYC verification through officially valid documents.

4.3.12
From a functional perspective, bidders may note that a single successful

onboarding may typically involve verification of multiple document types (identity, address, business/registration, authorization, and beneficial ownership-related documents), depending on the category and risk profile of the customer. The solution should be capable of supporting both individual and entity-level document verification workflows, including API-based validation with authoritative sources wherever applicable (e.g., PAN, Aadhaar, GSTIN, CKYC registry, etc.).

4.3.13
The above description provides an indicative and abstract understanding

of customer categories and document verification requirements. The exact set, number, and type of documents to be collected and verified for onboarding shall be governed by the applicable RBI Master Directions on
Page 6 of 26
KYC NABARD’s policy, guidelines, and regulatory instructions issued from time to time.

4.3.14
The bidder’s solution shall be configurable and scalable to accommodate
changes in regulatory guidelines, document requirements, onboarding workflows, and verification mechanisms, without significant
redevelopment effort.

4.3.15
The bidder may note that the number of documents required to be

verified for completion of KYC/KYB onboarding may vary depending on the type and risk profile of the customer. Indicatively, in case of individual customers under simplified or CKYC-based onboarding, the process may involve verification of minimum 2 to 3 document types (including Officially Valid Documents (OVDs), PAN/Form 60, or CKYC Identifier). In contrast, for non-individual entities such as companies, partnership firms, trusts, NGOs, Government bodies, and other juridical persons, the onboarding process may involve verification of multiple document categories, typically ranging up to 8–12 document types, including entity-level documents, authorization records, and KYC documents of beneficial owners and authorized signatories.

4.3.16
These numbers are indicative for estimation purposes only and are based

on NABARD’s policy, guidelines and RBI Master Directions on KYC. The actual number and type of documents required for onboarding shall depend on the applicable regulatory requirements, risk categorization, and nature of the customer/entity, and may vary from case to case. The bidder’s solution shall therefore be capable of configuring variable document sets dynamically and supporting verification of multiple documents through digital/manual and API-based mechanisms as required. NABARD reserves the right to modify document requirements in line with changes in internal policy or regulatory guidelines, and the solution shall accommodate such changes without significant
redevelopment.

The bidder shall note that while the solution is expected to support integration with authoritative sources and enable API-based or digital verification of documents wherever feasible (e.g., PAN, Aadhaar, CKYC, GSTIN, etc.), all documents involved in the onboarding process may not be digitally verifiable through trusted sources or APIs. Certain documents, particularly entity-level, authorization, or supporting documents (e.g., constitutional documents, resolutions, declarations, or project-related documents), may require manual verification or assisted validation workflows. Accordingly, the bidder’s solution shall be capable of supporting both digital/API-based verification and manual/assisted verification mechanisms, including document upload, review workflows, maker-checker controls, and audit trail generation, without restricting onboarding flows only to digitally verifiable documents. 4.3.17

sec.title: 4.4 Risk Profiling, Categorization & Periodic Update
sec.p:
4.4.1
The solution shall support capture and maintenance of KYC risk
categorization for customers/entities (e.g., Low/Medium/High and other policy driven categories such as “Not Required” where applicable) and
Page 7 of 26
shall expose the risk category for workflow routing, approvals, alerts and reporting.

4.4.2
The solution shall support risk-based ongoing due diligence, including

configurable periodic KYC update, Re-KYC schedules and triggers based on risk category, profile changes, document expiry, and policy updates, with system-generated alerts, tasks and exception handling.

4.4.3
The solution shall provide configurable and transparent risk-scoring

capabilities. For each risk classification assigned to a customer or entity, the solution shall provide an auditable explanation identifying the key factors contributing to the risk rating, including but not limited to customer profile, geography, beneficial ownership structure, PEP status, screening outcomes, and other configured risk parameters.

sec.title: 4.4.3.1 Enhanced Due Diligence for PEP Cases:
sec.p: The Bidder shall ensure that the proposed solution provides specific controls for customers identified as Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), including family members and close associates, as per applicable policy/regulatory requirements. The solution shall facilitate enhanced due diligence by enabling mandatory PEP flagging, collection of additional customer information and source-related details wherever required, routing for approval by the designated competent authority, enhanced and ongoing transaction monitoring, risk-based review at defined intervals, and generation of alerts/reports for compliance oversight. The solution shall preserve complete logs and audit trails of all PEP-related checks, approvals, status changes, reviews, and monitoring actions.

4.4.4
The solution should be capable of integrating with third-party credit
bureaus and external risk data providers, if required by NABARD, for supplementary risk assessment and due diligence activities.

4.4.5
The solution shall support separate workflows for “No change” and
“Change” cases during periodic update, including capture of self-declaration / confirmation from the customer or legal entity through registered email/mobile/letter or authorized communication.

4.4.6
For customers other than individuals (legal entities), the solution shall
support obtaining no-change declarations through authorized
communication (e.g., letter/board resolution as applicable) and shall ensure that Beneficial Ownership (BO) information is reviewed and updated where required during Re-KYC.

4.4.7
The solution shall provide dashboards/MIS for risk distribution,
due/overdue periodic update cases, and exceptions to support audit/inspection needs.

4.4.8
The solution shall support multi-layer Beneficial Ownership (UBO)
tracing, including recursive identification of ultimate natural persons based on configurable ownership thresholds.

4.5.2

4.5.3

sec.p: Bidder shall ensure masking, tokenization, anonymization, or equivalent protection of personal and sensitive data used in non-production environments. Any extraction, staging, migration, transformation, transport, backup, archival, or disposal of datasets during

implementation, testing, migration, cutover, rollback, stabilization, or support activities shall be carried out securely using encryption, controlled access, traceable handling, retention controls, and secure deletion procedures. The Bidder shall maintain documented controls for migration dataset handling and shall make such controls and audit evidence available to NABARD on request.

sec.title: 4.8 Aadhaar Vault Integration APIs (Tokenization + Masking Services)
sec.p:
4.8.1
The Bidder shall be responsible for providing an API based integration

layer (adapters/SDKs and integration patterns) to enable existing NABARD applications to consume Aadhaar Vault (ADV) services for tokenization (Reference Key generation), authorized detokenization, and masking services.

4.8.2
The Bidder shall ensure all Aadhaar number handling occurs only via the
ADV APIs/microservices; NABARD applications shall store and use only Reference Keys/tokens, and shall not store Aadhaar numbers or connected Aadhaar data outside the ADV.

4.8.3
The Bidder shall provide a masking service integration option, so
consuming applications can request masked outputs (e.g., only last digits) for UI display, logs, and exports, while ensuring raw Aadhaar is never exposed by default.

4.8.4
The Bidder shall implement end-to-end auditability for vault API calls,
including who/what system invoked tokenization/ de-
tokenization/masking, timestamps, purpose/context, and outcome.

4.8.5
The Bidder shall integrate Aadhaar vault services through trusted secure
communication channels and secure APIs/microservices, with
authenticated and authorized access and complete logging and monitoring.

4.8.6
The Bidder shall ensure de-tokenization (or any access that reveals raw
Aadhaar) is permitted only for explicitly authorized roles and approved applications, with maker-checker (where applicable) and full audit logging of purpose/context and outcome.

4.8.7
The Bidder shall ensure that masked identifiers are the default response
for UI display, logs, and exports; raw identifier access (if permitted) shall be exception-based, monitored, and audit-ready.

sec.title: 4.9 PAN Vault (Tokenization & Controlled Access)
sec.p:

The Bidder shall provide a secure PAN vault capability enabling
tokenization/aliasing, so downstream applications can reference tokens instead of storing raw PAN, with strict access controls and audit logging.

4.9.2
The Bidder shall enforce masking policies in UI/exports and maintain
audit logs for any access to raw PAN.
